findings.name: Enabled policy with no assigned users or groups
findings.description: An enabled Conditional Access policy applies to no users or groups.
findings.remediation: Assign the policy to the intended user or group scope, or disable/delete it if obsolete.

findings.name: Excluded groups in Conditional Access policy
findings.description: The policy excludes one or more groups.
findings.remediation: Verify the exclusion is still required. Document the business justification.

findings.name: Privileged roles not covered by MFA-requiring policy
findings.description: One or more privileged directory roles are NOT covered by a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA.
findings.remediation: Create or update a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all privileged directory roles.

findings.name: Break-glass account not properly excluded
findings.description: No break-glass account was detected in the exclusion list of MFA-requiring policies.
findings.remediation: Designate 1-2 cloud-only break-glass accounts and exclude them from all Conditional Access policies.

findings.name: Wide exclusion group (more than 20 members)
findings.description: A group with more than 20 members is excluded from a Conditional Access policy.
findings.remediation: Review group membership. Tighten to only the users who genuinely need the exclusion.

findings.name: No enabled policy blocks legacy authentication
findings.description: No enabled CA policy blocks legacy authentication protocols.
findings.remediation: Create a CA policy targeting legacy client app types with a Block grant control.

findings.name: Insufficient or absent CA enforcement
findings.description: Tenant has zero enabled CA policies, or fewer than 3.
findings.remediation: Enable baseline policies: require MFA for admins, block legacy auth, require MFA for all users.

findings.name: Conflicting Conditional Access policies
findings.description: Two enabled policies target overlapping users/apps with contradictory grant controls.
findings.remediation: Review both policies. Consolidate or narrow scope to avoid ambiguity.

findings.name: Admin policy uses weak authentication strength
findings.description: A policy targeting privileged roles uses an authentication strength weaker than phishing-resistant MFA.
findings.remediation: Upgrade authentication strength to phishing-resistant (FIDO2, certificate-based, Windows Hello for Business).

findings.name: Named location used in policy requires review
findings.description: A Conditional Access policy uses named or excluded locations.

findings.name: No sign-in frequency or session control enforced
findings.description: No enabled CA policy enforces a sign-in frequency or persistent browser session control. Long-lived sessions increase the risk of stolen token abuse.
findings.remediation: Add a sign-in frequency control (e.g., 1 hour for admins, 30 days for users) and disable persistent browser sessions on unmanaged devices.

findings.name: No device compliance or hybrid-join requirement
findings.description: No enabled CA policy requires a compliant or hybrid Azure AD joined device for access to corporate resources.
findings.remediation: Create a policy requiring compliant devices or Hybrid Azure AD join for all users accessing M365 apps.

findings.name: Guest and external users not restricted
findings.description: No enabled CA policy explicitly restricts guest/external user access. Guests may have broader access than intended.
findings.remediation: Create a policy requiring MFA and compliant devices for guest users, and consider blocking access from unmanaged devices.
